/-!
# Bass–Quillen conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
-/

namespace BassQuillenConjecture

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u v

/-- A commutative ring is regular Noetherian if it is Noetherian and its localization at every
prime ideal is a regular local ring. Regularity of a Noetherian local ring is expressed by equality
of its Krull dimension and the minimal number of generators of its maximal ideal. -/
def IsRegularNoetherian (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Prop :=
  ∃ _ : IsNoetherianRing A,
    ∀ (p : Ideal A) (_ : p.IsPrime),
      ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) =
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)).spanFinrank

/--
The **Bass–Quillen conjecture** states that, for every regular Noetherian commutative ring $A$,
every $n$, and every rank $r$, extension of scalars along
$A \to A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$ induces a bijection
$\operatorname{Vect}_r(A) \to \operatorname{Vect}_r(A[t_1, \ldots, t_n])$.

Equivalently, as stated here without a constant-rank restriction, every finitely generated
projective $A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$-module is isomorphic to the extension of a finitely generated
projective $A$-module. Injectivity follows by specializing every variable to zero.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (hA : IsRegularNoetherian A)
    (n : ℕ) (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P]
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P]
    [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P] :
    ∃ (M : Type max u v) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M)
      (_ : Module.Finite A M) (_ : Module.Projective A M),
      letI : Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⊗[A] M) :=
        TensorProduct.leftModule
      Nonempty (((MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] P) := by
  sorry

end BassQuillenConjecture

Stated the conjecture in its equivalent surjectivity form: every finitely generated projective module over the polynomial ring is extended from the base ring. Injectivity on isomorphism classes follows by specializing all variables to zero.
Quantified over all finitely generated projective modules instead of fixing a rank, so the statement remains faithful when Spec(A) is disconnected and rank is only locally constant.
Represented A[t₁,…,tₙ] as `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A`.

Represented scalar extension as `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M`, canonically equivalent to the source's `M ⊗_A A[t₁,…,tₙ]`; this orientation carries Mathlib's natural polynomial-ring module structure.

Defined regular Noetherian rings through the standard local criterion: A is Noetherian and every localization at a prime has Krull dimension equal to the minimal number of generators (`spanFinrank`) of its maximal ideal.

/-!

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
-/

namespace BassQuillenConjecture

universe u v

/--
A commutative ring is a regular local ring if it is Noetherian, has a unique maximal ideal,
and that ideal can be generated by as many elements as the Krull dimension of the ring.
-/
def IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop :=
  IsNoetherianRing R ∧
    ∃ m : Ideal R, m.IsMaximal ∧
      (∀ m' : Ideal R, m'.IsMaximal → m' = m) ∧
      ∃ s : Finset R, Ideal.span (s : Set R) = m ∧
        (s.card : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R

/--
A commutative ring is regular Noetherian if it is Noetherian and its localization at every
prime ideal is a regular local ring.
-/
def IsRegularNoetherianRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop :=
  IsNoetherianRing R ∧
    ∀ p : Ideal R, ∀ hp : p.IsPrime,
      let _ : Fact p.IsPrime := ⟨hp⟩
      IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)

/-- Extension of scalars of an `A`-module `M` to a commutative `A`-algebra `B`. -/
abbrev extensionOfScalars (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) : ModuleCat.{max u v} B :=
  @ModuleCat.of B _ (TensorProduct A B M) _ TensorProduct.leftModule

/--
The **Bass–Quillen conjecture** states that if $A$ is a regular Noetherian commutative ring,
then extension of scalars along $A \to A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ induces a bijection on isomorphism
classes of finitely generated projective modules (vector bundles) of each rank. Equivalently,
every finitely generated projective $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$-module is isomorphic to
$A[t_1,\ldots,t_n] \otimes_A M$ for a finitely generated projective $A$-module $M$.
This states the equivalent surjectivity formulation; injectivity follows by specializing every
$t_i$ to zero.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture :
    ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A], IsRegularNoetherianRing A →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (P : ModuleCat.{max u v} (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)),
        Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P →
        Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P →
        ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A,
          Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Projective A M ∧
            Nonempty (P ≅ extensionOfScalars A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) M) := by
  sorry

end BassQuillenConjecture

/-!
# Bass–Quillen conjecture

The Bass–Quillen conjecture relates vector bundles (finitely generated projective modules) over a
regular Noetherian ring $A$ and over the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$: it asserts that
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is a bijection on isomorphism classes.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- H. Bass, *Some problems in "classical" algebraic K-theory*, Algebraic K-Theory II,
  Lecture Notes in Math. 342, Springer (1973).
- D. Quillen, *Projective modules over polynomial rings*, Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 167–171.
-/

namespace BassQuillenConjecture

open TensorProduct

universe u v

/-- A local ring $R$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian
and $\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements, where $\dim R$ is the Krull dimension of
$R$. By Krull's height theorem every generating set of $\mathfrak{m}$ has at least $\dim R$
elements, so this says that the embedding dimension
$\dim_{R/\mathfrak{m}} \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$ of $R$ equals its Krull dimension. -/
def IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop :=
  IsNoetherianRing R ∧ ∃ s : Finset R, Ideal.span (s : Set R) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ∧
    (s.card : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R

/-- A commutative ring $A$ is a *regular Noetherian ring* if it is Noetherian and its localization
$A_{\mathfrak{p}}$ at every prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ is a regular local ring. -/
def IsRegularRing (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop :=
  IsNoetherianRing A ∧
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)

/-- A field is a regular local ring. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularLocalRing K :=
  ⟨inferInstance, ∅, by simp [IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_eq_bot], by
    simp [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field]⟩

/-- A field is a regular Noetherian ring. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularRing K := by
  refine ⟨inferInstance, fun p ↦ ?_⟩
  have hF : IsField (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) :=
    (RingEquiv.ofBijective _ ((Field.toIsField K).localization_map_bijective
      (M := p.asIdeal.primeCompl) (by simp))).symm.isField (Field.toIsField K)
  exact ⟨inferInstance, ∅, by simp [IsLocalRing.isField_iff_maximalIdeal_eq.mp hF],
    by simp [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField hF]⟩

-- Synthesising the `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A`-module structure on `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M`
-- exceeds the default instance budget.
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 100000 in
/--
**Bass–Quillen conjecture.** Let $A$ be a regular Noetherian ring and let $n \ge 0$. Then
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ induces a bijection from the set of isomorphism classes
of finitely generated projective $A$-modules to the set of isomorphism classes of finitely
generated projective $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$-modules. Concretely:
* (surjectivity) every finitely generated projective $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$-module $P$ is
  *extended* from $A$, i.e. $P \cong A[t_1, \dots, t_n] \otimes_A M$ for some finitely generated
  projective $A$-module $M$;
* (injectivity) if $A[t_1, \dots, t_n] \otimes_A M \cong A[t_1, \dots, t_n] \otimes_A M'$ for
  finitely generated projective $A$-modules $M$ and $M'$, then $M \cong M'$.

Here the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A`, and the
$A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$-module $A[t_1, \dots, t_n] \otimes_A M$ is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M`.
Wikipedia states the bijection rank by rank, as
$\operatorname{Vect}_r A \to \operatorname{Vect}_r (A[t_1, \dots, t_n])$ for every $r$; quantifying
over all finitely generated projective modules (of possibly non-constant rank) is equivalent, since
rank is preserved by extension and by the specialisation $t_i = 0$, and the idempotents of
$A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ are those of $A$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (hA : IsRegularRing A) (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P]
      [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P] [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P],
      ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M),
        Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Projective A M ∧
          Nonempty (P ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M)) ∧
    (∀ (M M' : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] [Module.Projective A M]
      [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module.Finite A M'] [Module.Projective A M'],
      Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A]
        MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M') →
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[A] M')) := by
  sorry

/--
**Quillen–Suslin theorem** (Serre's problem on projective modules). This is the case of the
Bass–Quillen conjecture in which $A = k$ is a field: every finitely generated projective module
over $k[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is free.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem quillen_suslin (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P]
    [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P] [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P]
    [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P] :
    Module.Free (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P := by
  sorry

end BassQuillenConjecture

This is equivalent: rank is preserved by extension and by specialisation t_i = 0, and idempotents of A[t_1,…,t_n] are those of A, so one reduces to constant rank by decomposing A. The decomposition-table notes explicitly permit this.
The tensor product is written as MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M (Mathlib's TensorProduct.leftModule gives the A[t]-module structure) rather than M ⊗_A A[t]; these are canonically isomorphic.

Universes: the polynomial-ring module P ranges over an arbitrary universe Type v; the A-modules M, M' range over the universe of A. Since all modules are finitely generated this loses no generality.

a regular Noetherian ring $A$ and over the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$: it predicts that
extension of scalars $M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is a bijection on isomorphism
classes, i.e. that every vector bundle over $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is extended from $A$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- H. Bass, *Some problems in "classical" algebraic K-theory*, Algebraic K-Theory II,
  Lecture Notes in Math. 342, Springer (1973).
- D. Quillen, *Projective modules over polynomial rings*, Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 167–171.
-/

open TensorProduct IsLocalRing

namespace BassQuillenConjecture

universe u

/-- A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension
$\dim R$ equals the dimension $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$ of its cotangent space over
the residue field $k = R/\mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements). -/
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop where
  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)

/-- A commutative ring `A` is *regular* if its localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at every prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ is a regular local ring. (This does not by itself force `A` to be Noetherian; the
Bass–Quillen conjecture is about regular *Noetherian* rings.) -/
class IsRegularRing (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)

/-- Every field is a regular local ring (of dimension $0$). -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularLocalRing K where
  isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
    rw [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field, finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero]
    rfl

/-- Every discrete valuation ring is a regular local ring (of dimension $1$). -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_isDiscreteValuationRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] : IsRegularLocalRing R where
  isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
    rw [IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one R (IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_isField R),
      finrank_CotangentSpace_eq_one]
    rfl

/-- Every field is a regular (Noetherian) ring, so the hypotheses of the Bass–Quillen conjecture
are satisfiable; for fields the conjecture is the Quillen–Suslin theorem. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularRing K where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization p _ := by
    have h0 : (0 : K) ∉ p.primeCompl := fun h ↦ h p.zero_mem
    have hK : IsField (Localization.AtPrime p) :=
      (RingEquiv.ofBijective _ (Field.localization_map_bijective h0)).symm.toMulEquiv.isField
        (Field.toIsField K)
    exact
      { isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
        ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
          rw [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField hK, finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero_iff.mpr hK]
          rfl }

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bass–Quillen conjecture

The Bass–Quillen conjecture relates vector bundles (i.e. finitely generated projective modules)
over a regular Noetherian ring $A$ and over the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$.

For a commutative ring $A$, write $\operatorname{Vect}_r A$ for the set of isomorphism classes of
finitely generated projective $A$-modules of (constant) rank $r$. The conjecture asserts that for
every regular Noetherian ring $A$, every $n$ and every $r$, base change
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Vect}_r A \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Vect}_r (A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]).$$
Equivalently, every finitely generated projective $A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$-module is *extended*
from $A$. The case where $A$ is a field is the Quillen–Suslin theorem.

Mathlib does not yet have regular local rings, so this file defines `IsRegularLocalRing`
(a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal can be generated by `dim R` elements) and
`IsRegularRing` (a Noetherian ring all of whose localizations at prime ideals are regular local
rings).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Bass–Quillen conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Quillen–Suslin theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillen%E2%80%93Suslin_theorem)
- H. Bass, *Some problems in "classical" algebraic K-theory*, Algebraic K-Theory II,
  Lecture Notes in Math. 342, Springer (1973).
- D. Quillen, *Projective modules over polynomial rings*, Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 167–171.
- T. Y. Lam, *Serre's problem on projective modules*, Springer Monographs in Mathematics (2006).
-/

namespace BassQuillenConjecture

open IsLocalRing TensorProduct

universe u

section RegularRings

/-- A commutative ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal
ideal can be generated by `dim R` elements, i.e. the minimal number of generators of the maximal
ideal equals the Krull dimension of `R`. -/
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop
    extends IsLocalRing R, IsNoetherianRing R where
  spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_ringKrullDim :
    ((maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R

/-- A commutative ring `A` is a *regular (Noetherian) ring* if it is Noetherian and its localization
at every prime ideal is a regular local ring. -/
class IsRegularRing (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing A where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)

/-- A field is a regular local ring (of dimension `0`). -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
instance instIsRegularLocalRingOfField (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularLocalRing K where
  spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_ringKrullDim := by
    simp [maximalIdeal_eq_bot, ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field]

/-- A ring which is a field is a regular local ring. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
lemma IsRegularLocalRing.of_isField {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (hR : IsField R) :
    IsRegularLocalRing R := by
  letI := hR.toField
  infer_instance

/-- A field is a regular ring. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
instance instIsRegularRingOfField (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularRing K where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization p := by
    have hp : p.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes K := by
      rw [minimalPrimes, Ideal.minimalPrimes_eq_subsingleton_self, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      exact Ideal.eq_bot_of_prime _
    have : Ring.KrullDimLE 0 (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) := .of_isLocalization _ hp _
    exact .of_isField Ring.KrullDimLE.isField_of_isReduced

end RegularRings

section VectorBundles

/-- A *vector bundle of rank `r`* over a commutative ring `A` is a finitely generated projective
`A`-module `M` whose rank at every prime ideal of `A` is `r`, i.e. `M` is an element of
$\operatorname{Vect}_r A$. -/
def IsVectorBundleOfRank (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Projective A M ∧
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, Module.rankAtStalk M p = r

/-- The free module `A ^ r` is a vector bundle of rank `r`. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
lemma isVectorBundleOfRank_pi_fin (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Nontrivial A] (r : ℕ) :
    IsVectorBundleOfRank A (Fin r → A) r :=
  ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance, fun p ↦ by simp⟩

end VectorBundles

section Conjecture

variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularRing A] (n : ℕ)

-- Typeclass search for the `A[t₁, …, tₙ]`-module structure on `A[t₁, …, tₙ] ⊗[A] M` is slow,
-- so raise the limit in this section.
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 100000

/-- **Bass–Quillen conjecture.**
Let $A$ be a regular Noetherian ring and $n, r \geq 0$. Then base change
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Vect}_r A \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Vect}_r (A[t_1, \ldots, t_n])$$
between the isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules of rank $r$ over $A$ and
over $A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$.

The bijection is spelled out on representatives: the map is injective (two rank `r` vector
bundles over `A` whose base changes to `A[t_1, …, t_n]` are isomorphic are already isomorphic)
and surjective (every rank `r` vector bundle over `A[t_1, …, t_n]` is, up to isomorphism, the
base change of a rank `r` vector bundle over `A`, i.e. is *extended* from `A`). -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture (r : ℕ) :
    (∀ (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N],
      IsVectorBundleOfRank A M r → IsVectorBundleOfRank A N r →
      Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A]
        MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] N) →
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[A] N)) ∧
    (∀ (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P],
      IsVectorBundleOfRank (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P r →
      ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M), IsVectorBundleOfRank A M r ∧
        Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] P)) := by
  sorry

/-- **Bass–Quillen conjecture**, in the form in which it is usually stated (Bass, Quillen, Lam):
if $A$ is a regular Noetherian ring, then every finitely generated projective
$A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$-module $P$ is *extended* from $A$, i.e. there is a finitely generated
projective $A$-module $M$ with $P \cong M \otimes_A A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$.

This is equivalent to `bass_quillen_conjecture` for all `r`: injectivity of
$\operatorname{Vect}_r A \to \operatorname{Vect}_r (A[t_1, \ldots, t_n])$ is automatic (specialize
$t_i = 0$), and base change preserves the rank at every prime. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture.variants.extended
    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P]
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P] [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P] :
    ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M), Module.Finite A M ∧
      Module.Projective A M ∧
      Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] P) := by
  sorry

/-- **Quillen–Suslin theorem** (Serre's problem), the case of the Bass–Quillen conjecture where
$A = k$ is a field: every finitely generated projective $k[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$-module is free. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture.variants.quillen_suslin (k : Type*) [Field k]
    (P : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P]
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P] [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P] :
    Module.Free (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) P := by
  sorry

end Conjecture

end BassQuillenConjecture

The zero ring is vacuously regular; the conjecture is trivial for it.

Vect_r A is modelled by the predicate `IsVectorBundleOfRank A M r := Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Projective A M ∧ ∀ p, Module.rankAtStalk M p = r` (constant rank r at every prime), rather than by a quotient type of isomorphism classes.

The bijection is unpacked on representatives instead of constructing the set of isomorphism classes: (injective) for rank-r bundles M, N over A, an A[t]-linear isomorphism A[t] ⊗[A] M ≃ A[t] ⊗[A] N yields M ≃ₗ[A] N; (surjective) every rank-r bundle P over A[t] admits a rank-r bundle M over A with A[t] ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[A[t]] P. Isomorphisms are expressed as `Nonempty (_ ≃ₗ[_] _)`.
Base change is written in Mathlib's convention `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M` (with `TensorProduct.leftModule`) rather than Wikipedia's `M ⊗_A A[t_1,…,t_n]`; these are canonically isomorphic.
The polynomial ring A[t_1,…,t_n] is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` with n : ℕ (n = 0 allowed, trivially true).

All module types are quantified in the universe `u` of A (`M N P : Type u`, `∃ M : Type u`). This loses nothing since every finitely generated module is isomorphic to one in the universe of the base ring; it avoids universe issues in the existential.

The section uses `set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 100000` because Mathlib's instance search for `Module (MvPolynomial σ A) (MvPolynomial σ A ⊗[A] M)` first explores the dead end `MvPolynomial.module` (needing `Module (MvPolynomial σ A) A`) before finding `TensorProduct.leftModule`; the resulting instance is the standard one (verified with `exact?`).

Two extra declarations are included as variants (not slots): `bass_quillen_conjecture.variants.extended` (every f.g. projective A[t_1,…,t_n]-module is extended from A — the usual literature form, research open) and `bass_quillen_conjecture.variants.quillen_suslin` (A a field: every f.g. projective k[t_1,…,t_n]-module is free, research solved). API/test lemmas: fields are regular local rings and regular rings; A^r is a rank-r vector bundle (needs `Nontrivial A`).

/-- **Bass–Quillen conjecture.**
Let $A$ be a regular Noetherian ring and $n, r \geq 0$. Then base change
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Vect}_r A \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Vect}_r (A[t_1, \ldots, t_n])$$
between the isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules of rank $r$ over $A$ and
over $A[t_1, \ldots, t_n]$.

The bijection is spelled out on representatives: the map is injective (two rank `r` vector
bundles over `A` whose base changes to `A[t_1, …, t_n]` are isomorphic are already isomorphic)
and surjective (every rank `r` vector bundle over `A[t_1, …, t_n]` is, up to isomorphism, the
base change of a rank `r` vector bundle over `A`, i.e. is *extended* from `A`). -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture (r : ℕ) :
    (∀ (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N],
      IsVectorBundleOfRank A M r → IsVectorBundleOfRank A N r →
      Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A]
        MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] N) →
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[A] N)) ∧
    (∀ (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P],
      IsVectorBundleOfRank (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P r →
      ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M), IsVectorBundleOfRank A M r ∧
        Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] P)) := by
